messages:
Riley: Quick question — we keep getting reports from infra that billing attribution sometimes shows the org of the proxy service instead of the original service-account when requests go through the routing proxy. Is this the auth resolver or the routing layer?
Priya: Most likely an attribution resolution issue. Routing preserves the original token but the billing lookup currently reads token issuer from the proxy header.
Sam: Are we standardizing on an "effective_owner" field anywhere? I thought console dashboards already use it but maybe not consistently.
Marco: Console uses the token claim if present, otherwise falls back to X-Forwarded-Project. The proxy sets X-Forwarded-Project to the node pool owner for routing purposes.
Riley: That fallback is the problem — when service accounts impersonate across projects we lose the original project in billing. Example: svc-a@project-A impersonates svc-b@project-B via proxy -> billing shows project-A (proxy) instead of project-B.
Casey: Oof. That explains the spike in unexpected billing. Do we have telemetry to surface effective vs observed owner?
Priya: Not end-to-end. We log the raw token claim at the auth resolver and the routing header at the edge, but no canonical "effective_owner" event that ties them together in traces.
Sam: Proposal: introduce an auth-resolver output header `X-Redwood-Effective-Owner: project-B:svc-b` emitted by auth service and passed through router. Console + billing use that header as canonical, with a verification step.
Marco: Implementation detail: router currently strips unknown headers. We'll need to whitelist `X-Redwood-*` or inject it after routing decisions. Also need to sign the header to avoid spoofing.
Riley: +1 on signing. Could be HMAC with auth-resolver key, and router validates signature before adding to request context.
Priya: Telemetry: emit an event `auth.effective_owner` with fields: original_claim, resolved_owner, resolver_version. That will let us track mismatches.
Sam: UX: Console should show both reported owner and effective owner, with a diff marker and link to the trace that shows the path. We should also add a small badge indicating when billing uses effective_owner vs proxy fallback.
Casey: Rollout plan thoughts? This is user-visible for billing. We should be extremely careful.
Marco: Rolling out as opt-in first via a feature-flag header `X-RW-Auth-Resolver=on` for a small % of traffic. Monitor three signals: 401s, attribution drift %, and billing delta.
Riley: Agreed. Also add a canary that maps requests from internal CI/jobs so we can validate with known traffic before any customer traffic changes.
Priya: Back-compat: if signature verification fails, router should fall back to current behavior and emit `auth.resolver_sig:fail` metric.
Sam: Metrics to add: `auth.effective_owner.mismatch.count`, `auth.resolver_sig.fail.count`, `billing.attribution.overrides.count`. Also include tag for resolver_version and rollout_flag.
Casey: For dashboards: new per-model/per-route panel showing attribution heatmap: rows=observed_owner, cols=effective_owner, color=tokens. Filterable by date and rollout flag.
Marco: On the API surface, I want to avoid changing the public token format. This is purely internal header plumbing.
Riley: Security check — can a malicious proxy inject `X-Redwood-Effective-Owner`? That's why we sign it and only trust signature from our auth-resolver key stored in KMS.
Priya: I'll draft a minimal HMAC scheme: header `X-Redwood-Effective-Owner: project:svc`, `X-Redwood-Eo-Sig: sha256=hex(hmac(secret, header_value|ts))`, and `X-Redwood-Eo-Ts`. Router validates ts within 60s and signature.
Sam: Sounds good. Also think about rotation: key id header so we can rotate without breaking. `X-Redwood-Eo-Kid`.
Casey: Who owns the console UX change? Product or DevEx? We need small mocks before infra teams implement headers.
Riley: Product (Casey) + DevEx (Sam) to mock, Infra (Marco) + Auth (Priya) to implement. I'll create an RFC and assign owners.
Marco: Small snippet for router validation (pseudo):
```
val = req.header("X-Redwood-Effective-Owner")
sig = req.header("X-Redwood-Eo-Sig")
kid = req.header("X-Redwood-Eo-Kid")
if !validate_sig(kid, val, sig, ts):
  emit_metric("auth.resolver_sig.fail")
  passthrough()
else:
  ctx.effective_owner = parse(val)
```
Sam: We should also store the effective_owner in traces: `trace.set_attr("auth.effective_owner", val)` so console links can deep dive.
Priya: I'll add a small test matrix in the auth-resolver repo: cases for impersonation, token exchange, expired ts, bad sig, kid rotation.
Casey: Timeline: can we get a draft RFC + mocks by EOD Friday? I want to brief billing next week.
Riley: EOD Friday for RFC + mocks is tight but doable. Priya + Sam + Casey take it. I'll book a quick sync Tue to review metrics.
deploy-bot: Riley scheduled a meeting: "Auth attribution sync" on Tue 10:00 — invites sent.
Sam: Action items: Priya implement header + signing, Marco whitelist header and validate sig, Casey + Sam mock console and dashboard, Riley own RFC and rollout plan.
Casey: Thanks all — I'll start mocks and ping @sam for console APIs.
Priya: Starting an internal PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/auth-resolver/pull/427 — WIP
Riley: Great. Let's keep the rollout conservative. If metrics show any spike, we rollback the feature-flag. :thumbsup:
